title: Supported-Hom pair and evaluation-normalized identification
statement: Use the small-site size convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a commutative ring $A$ in universe $u+1$, a supported-Hom pair consists of a site with object universe $u+1$ and morphism universe $u$, sheafification and a Grothendieck abelian category of $A$-module sheaves, a terminal object $T$, an object $W$ and arrow $W\to T$, a sheaf $B$, and a restriction $A_T\to B$ from the constant rank-one sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use the existing kernel-of-restriction sections and bounded-below right-derived supported groups of [def-pur-support-cohomology] in the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Its degree-$a$ derived-Hom model is $\operatorname{Hom}(B[0],K[a])$. An Identification consists of additive equivalences from the actual supported groups to these Hom groups, natural in bounded-below $K$, satisfying the evaluation-at-one cocycle normalization of [def-pur-supported-hom-cocycle-data]: on each bounded-below degreewise injective $I$, a closed $f:B\to I^a$ corresponds to the supported cycle whose kernel inclusion is the evaluation at one of $A_T\to B\xrightarrow f I^a$, and its cohomology class maps to the canonically localized single-complex cocycle of $f$. This is data with a specified normalization, not an existence assertion. For the finite datum $P$ of [def-pur-conventions] and a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], define the etale and pro-etale pairs by their actual small sites, terminal $X$, complement $X\setminus Z$, supported sheaf $i_*A_Z$, and canonical coefficient restriction; use comparison inverse image for pro-etale constants.
